thread.title: Berkshire Hathaway Shares Jump in Early Trading as Repurchase Program Makes Stock Attractive

author: MT Newswires
title: Berkshire Hathaway Shares Jump in Early Trading as Repurchase Program Makes Stock Attractive
text:
Shutterstock photo Berkshire Hathaway ( BRK.A ) shares jumped on Wednesday after the company announced it would amend its share repurchase program, giving investors hope that they'll be able to get their hands on some of the cash the company's been holding.
The company's prior policy on repurchases was that they wouldn't exceed a 20% premium over the current book value. Under an amendment adopted by the board of directors, Chief Executive Warren Buffett and Vice Chairman Charlie Munger can offer repurchases if they believe the price is below Berkshire's intrinsic value.
"The current policy whereby share repurchases will not be made if they would reduce the value of Berkshire's consolidated cash, cash equivalents and US Treasury Bills holdings below $20 billion will continue," the company said in a statement. "Berkshire will not initiate any share repurchases under the amended program until it publicly releases its second quarter earnings" on Aug. 3.
Berkshire A shares rose 4.3% and B shares were up 4.6% in early trading Wednesday.
Berkshire's cash holdings have exceeded $100 billion for three straight quarters through the first quarter of 2018, according to filings with the Securities and Exchange Commission. The company held almost $109 billion at the end of the first three months of the year.
Morgan Stanley on Wednesday said the new buyback policy allows the company to return excess capital to shareholders while maintaining flexibility to make acquisitions. Berkshire will report earnings after the close on Aug. 3, and solid results and ensuing stock repurchases should be positive for the stock, the bank said.
"We estimate strong second-quarter net income of $11.1 billion, aided by $5.5 billion after-tax gain in its equity investment portfolio, largely due to appreciation in Apple ( AAPL ) and Wells Fargo ( WFC )," Morgan Stanley said.
